reader.requirement: At --std 85 a CH/CF operand (data-name or FINAL, which the 1985 format requires to be written) must name an operand of the RD's CONTROL clause (qualified spellings naming the same item included), at most one CH and one CF may exist per control data-name or FINAL, and a control with no CH or CF is legal.

refuses the optional ON/FOR word before the operand below COBOL-2002
refuses a reference-modified TYPE operand below COBOL-2002; qualification stays admitted
EditionContext.SubscriptedClauseOperands (Year == 2002) admits a subscripted operand; 85 refuses it

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the operand is required and ON/FOR, OR PAGE and reference modification are refused (later editions admit them); the membership test (SR10) and the one-CH/one-CF-per-level census (SR14) are the same code at every edition.

reader.notes: ResolveReports resolves each CH/CF operand to a control level (FINAL by FindIndex, data-name by ControlLevelOf, qualifier-insensitive) and refuses a miss; the census refuses a second CH or CF per level. The 1985 operand forms are gated in VersionConformancePass (format diagram read from the transcription; the scan lacks XIII-55, transcribed from GovInfo). The COBOL0899 for a non-control operand is positioned at the RD line, not the group entry, and cites §2023 (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: Membership and count halves hold: xrptctl.cob (R1 CONTROL WS-A, R2 CONTROL WS-B, R2 CH WS-A) refused COBOL0899 'RD R2: the TYPE CH operand WS-A shall be the same as one of the operands of the CONTROL clause'; wrongitem.cob (CONTROL WS-KEY OF G1, CH WS-KEY OF G2, a different item of the same name) refused COBOL0899; ControlLevelOf matches the written reference first, then the resolved item. The doubt is the qualified operand the reader's requirement admits: qualneedless.cob (WS-KEY unique, CONTROL IS WS-KEY, TYPE CH WS-KEY OF WS-GRP) compiles and runs EXIT 0 at --std 85, as did the reader's chqual.cob (CF WS-KEY IN WS-GRP). The 1985 text: 'OK  §1985:III.2  (2. DEFINITIONS)  the text is in the clause' -- a 'data-name' in a general format 'must not be reference-modified, subscripted, or qualified unless specifically permitted by the rules of the format'; the CONTROL clause permits it ('OK  §1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR1 ... the text is in SR1', 'Data-name-1 may be qualified'), but no TYPE syntax rule does ('OK  §1985:XIII.3.20.3 SR4 ... the text is in SR4' says only 'must be specified in the CONTROL clause'). The compiler admits the qualified TYPE operand by a recorded READING (VersionConformancePass#GateCobol85ControlName doc comment; kb/Work PB5573 2026-11-14-landed.md: 'a QUALIFIED TYPE operand stays COBOL-85 ... a reading, folio XIII-55 missing, kb/Work PB4952'), that SR4's 'specified in the CONTROL clause' carries the CONTROL clause's qualified spelling. On the literal text the qualified operand is not permitted (under-rejects); on the recorded reading it is. The printed folio XIII-55 settles it. Nothing else in this rule's range failed.
refuter.corrected: Under the literal §1985:III.2 reading the verdict is PARTIAL (under-rejects): TYPE CH/CF data-name written qualified (qualneedless.cob, chqual.cob) is admitted at --std 85 though no TYPE rule permits qualification. Under PB5573's recorded reading (SR4 inherits the CONTROL clause's qualified spelling) CONFORMS stands.

adjudication.reason: Batch 23 ruling: the refuter confirmed SR4's membership and count halves (xrptctl.cob, wrongitem.cob refused), so SR4 CONFORMS; its doubt, a qualified TYPE operand compiling at 85, is upheld as a defect of the FORMAT row 1985-FMT-XIII.3.20.2 (kb/Work PB5910), not of SR4
